name: Workexe SEO Suite
tagline: An all-in-one SEO toolkit: technical site audits, on-page checks, keyword and rank tracking, reporting.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Half of an SEO suite is a crawler with opinions, and a crawler with opinions is exactly the kind of thing an agent writes well in an afternoon: fetch every URL on the sitemap, check titles, meta descriptions, headings, canonicals, alt text, status codes, redirect chains, orphan pages, page weight. That part you get, and for one site you own it is genuinely enough. The half you do not get is data you do not have: keyword search volumes, difficulty scores, backlink indexes, and SERP positions across locations and devices. Those come from either a licensed data vendor or a scraping fleet that fights Google for a living, and neither is a weekend. Build the auditor, rent the numbers, and accept that your dashboard will be uglier.
coreLoopDIY: Crawls your own site on a schedule, flags technical and on-page SEO problems, and writes a diffable report so you can see what changed since last week.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine or small VPS to run the crawler
A site you actually control, so crawling it is not rude
Optional: a SERP API key if you want real rank positions
Optional: a keyword data API if you want volumes, which is the part you cannot fake
whatYouLose: Keyword volume and difficulty numbers, which come from purchased or scraped clickstream data you do not have
A backlink index, which means no link audits, no competitor link gap, no toxic link flags
Rank tracking at scale across geographies and devices without getting your IP blocked
Competitor benchmarking, since it only knows about your site
Scheduled client-ready PDF reports and anyone to complain to when a number looks wrong
moatNotes: The crawler is commodity. The index behind the keyword and backlink tabs is the product, and it costs money every single day it stays fresh.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the interesting SEO questions are comparative. Not "is my title tag too long", which your own script answers, but "who outranks me for this and why, and what would it cost to catch them". Answering that needs a keyword corpus, a link graph, and daily SERP snapshots from a lot of IP addresses, and paying someone twenty or forty dollars a month for access to all three is much cheaper than building any one of them. Agencies also pay for the export button, because clients want a document, not a terminal.
notes: The audit half is a solved problem you can own outright; the data half is a subscription no matter whose logo is on it.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted SEO auditor for a single website I own. Stack: Node 20 with TypeScript, undici for fetching, cheerio for HTML parsing, better-sqlite3 for storage, and a plain Express server rendering server-side HTML with no frontend framework. No accounts, no telemetry, no cloud services.

CLI command `audit <start-url>`:
- Discover URLs from robots.txt and sitemap.xml, then crawl same-origin links up to a configurable max page count and concurrency.
- Respect robots.txt, send a clear custom user agent, and rate limit by default.
- For each page record: final URL, status code, redirect chain, response time, byte size, title, meta description, canonical, robots meta, h1 and h2 list, word count, image count, images missing alt text, internal and external link counts, hreflang tags, Open Graph tags, and structured data blocks found.
- Store every crawl as a timestamped run in SQLite so runs can be compared.

Issue rules engine in one file, each rule a small pure function with a severity and a human explanation: missing or duplicate titles, titles outside 15 to 60 characters, missing or duplicate meta descriptions, missing h1, multiple h1, 4xx and 5xx pages, redirect chains longer than one hop, non-canonical pages linked internally, orphan pages present in the sitemap but not linked, images missing alt text, pages over a size budget, and mixed content links.

Web UI on localhost: run list, per-run issue summary grouped by severity, a filterable page table, a single page detail view, and a diff view showing issues introduced or resolved versus the previous run.

Optional and gated behind env vars in .env, skipped cleanly when absent: SERP_API_KEY to fetch daily positions for a keywords.txt list, stored and charted over time. Do not scrape Google directly.

Explicitly out of scope: keyword volume estimates, keyword difficulty scores, backlink data, competitor analysis, PDF export, multi-user access. Do not fake these with made-up numbers or placeholder values; if data is unavailable, say so in the UI.

Ship a README with setup, a single `npm run audit` example, and a cron line for weekly runs.
